scope: All first ten completed normal main-evaluation videos, frames 0/20/40/60/80; three matched-caption reference panels. This is sampled-frame visual review, not full-video certification or a 40-case score.

VP001.observed: Athlete and sports setting are present, but body/limbs change irregularly across the airborne and landing states. Extra thin structures appear near the body. A flawed landing requested by the prompt does not justify unstable anatomy.

VP002.observed: A hand and wooden strip remain visible. Late frames contain extra intersecting wooden pieces; the single strip does not form the requested continuous bow.

VP003.observed: Gymnast, mat and clothing remain recognizable. The sampled sequence ends lying across the mat rather than landing cleanly on both feet; the middle body configuration is implausible.

VP004.observed: The ruler and fingers remain recognizable and a crack develops. The sampled frames do not establish bending under force preceding the fracture; late edges and fracture surface are irregular.
VP004.partial_success: visible object and fracture rather than a blank scene

VP005.observed: Paddle, ball and table remain recognizable, with a round ball in the later samples. Five frames alone do not verify a correct impact or trajectory.
VP005.partial_success: main objects and ball shape retained in sampled frames

VP006.observed: The canvas dominates the frame with yellow/brown blur and weak texture; the intended twisting action and removal of excess paint are not clearly represented.

VP007.observed: Large flat colored court regions dominate early frames; later objects are flattened circular discs rather than stable ping pong balls in a rally.

VP008.observed: Trampoline and lower body remain recognizable. Cropping and five-frame sampling prevent a confident assessment of whole-body geometry and rhythmic timing.
VP008.issue: not yet a verified process pass

VP009.observed: Worker, glass-like surface and adhered picture remain present. The tool changes shape and position while the surface stays essentially in place in the samples; no convincing suction-based panel lifting is established.

VP010.observed: Floor and mop are present, but the mop leaves the frame and later views contain mostly floor. The causal removal of the puddle is not clear from these five frames.
VP010.partial_success: recognizable scene rather than total visual corruption

references.scope: Same captions; R-series protocols recorded in the manifest. PhysVid is a different model/settings qualitative reference, not a controlled architectural ablation.
references.VP002: R18E, R19DT and R20AT all introduce extra slats/branching; R18G retains a more stable double-arch shape, but not a clear single-strip bending process. PhysVid preserves wood texture and continuous loop structures with little visible change. No unconditional visual winner is inferred.
references.VP004: R18E shows a badly deformed blue ruler, R18G a stable ruler with no clear fracture, DT a mostly straight ruler with a crack. R20AT retains the object and introduces a crack but does not convincingly solve the bend-then-fracture process. PhysVid also does not establish the requested ruler bending in these sampled frames.
references.VP009: PhysVid has clearer glass/device identity; R18G has a more stable suction disc. R18E/DT have changing tools, and R20AT still lacks a stable tool-plus-lift interaction. Keeping the person in view is insufficient for success.

interpretation: The current A design has not yet resolved the required structural/process quality; its successful training and noncollapsed intermediate C cannot establish that it has.

Several failure motifs recur across different physical executors. Same-checkpoint no-C and direct-only controls are needed to distinguish learned base/LoRA behavior from the contribution of the new physical write.
A stable or detailed frame alone does not establish physical improvement; static/no-process outputs are not a successful replacement.
Do not infer a RoPE bug, sampler bug, or a single cause from these images. Preserve the fixed evaluation inputs and obtain the already scheduled paired controls.
Continue the submitted main40+20 and necessary paired16 pipeline. Do not submit R20BT or change the running design based only on this first-ten view.
